message:
fix(ka-pc r6): the owner fence as one gate under one lock -- one consistent verdict, no write but a counted release after it (Codex F1, F2, T1)

- OwnerFenceGate (viewer_control_state.hpp) + viewer_owner_fence.hpp: the fence is raised FIRST, its baseline taken in
  the same critical section; the control thread takes an input off the queue and counts it (taken, in flight, release)
  in one critical section -- the scheduler's pick runs inside it (gate_begin_action), the fenced branch's
  gate_take_release too; the verdict reads queue, in-flight, counters and baseline in one critical section (F1)
- every control write of the loop goes through FenceGatedLink: after the fence only a counted release's exchange may
  start a write; refused writes are never started (the clipboard copy the sender already held is zeroed either way);
  bulk image / file datagrams are refused by the gate; a failure caused by a refusal goes back to the release-only
  branch, never to a resume or the end of the loop; a resume under way stops at the fence, begin_control_resume
  refuses after it, the resume probe writes through the gate; the fence no longer joins the image / file workers
  (the session teardown does) -- it refuses their sends at once (F2)
- the release-only take checks the release rule itself (the shared core's release_identity rule) and the same
  logon-screen gates as any input (r7 H6 / r9, held-back downs); a skipped one is counted as not sent
- test build only: REMOTE60_VIEWER_TEST_REFUSE_RELEASE_WRITE_AFTER_FENCE refuses the first release WRITE after the fence
  (no byte leaves) -- replacing r5's hook, which only flipped a finished exchange's result
- ka_pc_fence_test: F1 on Codex's schedule with a real stalled sender thread -- r5 (verbatim) Confirmed, r6 Pending then
  Failed; F2 -- r5 writes the held clipboard after the fence, r6 refuses it, refuses a pick and a down, admits a
  release; ka_pc_shell_logic_test: the exact test-tmp boundary and a new run folder of its own (T1)
